title: Buttermilk Brown Sugar Waffles
changes_from_base: A quick one-bowl buttermilk batter sweetened only with light brown sugar and raised with both baking powder and bicarbonate; no whisked whites, no fruit or cream.
summary: Classic buttermilk waffles sweetened lightly with brown sugar for a deep, caramel-edged flavour.
equipment: wire rack set in a rimmed baking tray

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
butter or oil spray, for the iron

steps.title: Whisk wet
steps.text: Whisk 2 eggs, 420 ml buttermilk and 113 g cooled melted butter together in a large bowl.

steps.title: Mix dry
steps.text: Stir 220 g plain flour, 2 tbsp light brown sugar, 2 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp bicarbonate of soda and 1 tsp fine salt in a second bowl.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Add the dry mix to the egg mixture and whisk only until smooth, then let the batter rest a few minutes.

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Heat the waffle iron and butter or spray it lightly, even if it is non-stick.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Ladle about 60 ml batter into a 20 cm round iron, or more for a larger one, and cook until light golden brown.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Serve at once with 60 ml maple syrup.

tips: Whisk the batter only until smooth, as overmixing will make the waffles tough.
Butter or spray the iron before every waffle, since even non-stick plates need it.
Adjust the amount of batter to suit the size of your iron, using more for larger rounds.
storage: This batter is meant to be cooked and served straight away for the best texture, so avoid leaving waffles to sit before serving. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
